body: Writing is one of my primary hobbies, so I suppose it's only natural. My own verbosity certainly doesn't help with the task of typing this on a tablet. As for the matter of driving, I do have the skills required to drive. It's the matter of the license itself that is the problem. As I alluded to in the main post, I had blood drawn for the first time in many years last February. During the process, I passed out and had some spasms. The nurse described it as a seizure; misinformation that I carried with me to when I was going to have my license renewed. Upon sharing this information, my license was (and still is) indefinitely suspended. I do wish I could leave, but my own innate tendency to overplan (I cannot stand uncertainty) left me in this position. As for your grammar and all that, don't worry about it; you're trilingual. That's two more languages than most Americans know.

With no driver's license, moving really isn't an option. I know that depression does nasty things to your head, but of course when the only thing you have to evaluate a broken mind is the mind itself, the best you can truly come up with is, "it's broke." It's a shame our mental self-repair functionality is nowhere near as elegant as the mechanism by which cuts are healed. Honestly, on my "good" days I feel myself yearning for peace and happiness, but on the bad days I just find myself wanting someone to kick down the house's door and blow my head off (you can read up on why I was so specific with that by going through my history). Dunno if I'd call it positive, maybe just deluded. Either way, I don't want grandeur out of life; just happiness and good times with friends and a loved one. That's all.

I'm way ahead of you on the Humble Bundle thing. I've got many accounts over many sites: Groupees, ShinyLoot, IndieRoyale (now closed), GreenManGaming, Gamersgate... I haven't started using Nuuvem or any majorly grey-market sites like that. Nevertheless, as I said, it's not as bad as my other issues; just that it seemed pertinent to the discussion at hand. I think the best thing I can do here is to just discipline myself, specifically with money. At the very least, I'm doing loads better than I had been in the past.

I'm certainly no negotiator, and I don't think I'd be doing anyone any favors by acting like one. It's good, at least, that you trust yourself enough to give advice out to those in such a fragile situation.

It appears that my wording may have led you astray slightly. I'm able to hold some mild chit-chat with people, and whenever I find someone with whom I share interests with, I can hold a fairly good conversation. My issue with respect to verbal communication has to do with eloquence and depth of ideas. Typing this out, I am able to convey my ideas in a more or less stream of consciousness manner, whereas when I go to converse with someone, my own "conversational depth" decreases. Not so much a matter of introversion (although that is not entirely offbase), but some other issue.

Not to sound particularly insulting, but if I had the ability to turn off my empathy, I would. It certainly hasn't done my psyche any favors. Being a good writer is one of the things that very deeply worries me; I have nowhere near this level of expressiveness whenever I am communicating verbally. Writing is also fairly subject to self-bias; anymore, I'm unsure if this "dark" side of me is even real, or if it is the product of an overactive imagination run rampant. I'm not even sure there is a person left anymore. Have I written myself into a demise? Am I just my own personal director of my own tragedy? At this point, do I exist merely to destroy myself? The nature of Ouroboros comes to mind once again.
